ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, registered shareholders, signatories, beneficial owners, and authorized agents against the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) consolidated financial sanctions list incorporating UN Security Council resolutions, EU/OFAC targeted sanctions, UK HMT sanctions where applicable, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, and the OFAC specially designated nationals (SDN) list. Enhanced due diligence and PEP status determination must follow FINMA Circular 2023/1, the AMLA and its implementing ordinances, including requirements for adverse media checks, source-of-wealth verification, and senior-management escalation for any PEP or sanctioned counterparty.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Zentraler Firmenindex (www.zefix.admin.ch) and the cantonal commercial registry (Handelsregisteramt) via the Swiss Federal business register portal (CH Register, www.uid.admin.ch or eGR-based cantonal systems).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name may be in any language provided it uses Latin letters and is not misleading. Where the name is derived from a non-Latin script, a Latin-alphabet transliteration must be submitted. The name must distinguish the company from all previously registered names, must not violate Swiss public policy, and must include the legal form suffix 'AG' or 'SA'. Official languages of the commercial register are German, French, and Italian; Romansh is accepted in certain cantons.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the commercial registry rejects a proposed name, the applicant must first file a written rectification request or resubmission with the same registry within the reservation period or within 30 days after receiving the rejection notice. A formal administrative appeal (Verfügungsbeschwerde) must then be filed with the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority (Handelsregisteraufsichtsbehörde) in the canton where the registered office is to be located. The appeal must state the legal basis and factual grounds. A further appeal on questions of law may lie to the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) within 30 days of the cantonal decision. All filings must be supported by a Swiss sworn translation if written in a foreign language.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office (shared administrative address with physical premises managed by a corporate services provider) is acceptable only as a registered seat for administrative functions, provided the company has access to the physical location and mail forwarding. For manufacturing of electric cargo bicycles under ISIC 3091, a virtual-only mailbox without any physical facility will not satisfy commercial substance requirements, social-security obligations, value-added tax registration, or cantonal business permits. The company must maintain tangible production, warehousing, or assembly premises in Switzerland, or must appoint a licensed Swiss manufacturing subcontractor with physical premises.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 15–20% annual probability of an unannounced safety and health inspection by SUVA/SECO during active manufacturing operations; 20–25% probability of a cantonal or federal tax audit during the first three years; 10% probability of an unannounced municipal or cantonal business-license inspection at the registered office to verify substantive office presence. The likelihood increases if the registered office is at a mass-directory service address.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Arts. 620–621, 626, 640, 643, 716b; Company Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV), Arts. 2, 5, 6.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce); federal coordination through Zefix and the Federal Commercial Registry platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (Statuten / Statuts) and application for registration in the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Eintragung ins Handelsregister).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: CHF 100,000 minimum share capital; at least CHF 50,000 must be paid in at incorporation and each share must be paid up to no less than 20% of its nominal amount. The paid-up funds are held in a blocked Swiss bank or postal account and are released only upon commercial registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The board, having verified the subscriptions, accepts the full subscription of CHF 100,000 share capital in accordance with the articles. The registered office is fixed at the address stated in the deed. The board appoints [Chairperson], [Chief Executive Officer], and [AML Compliance Officer] as first officers, each accepting office subject to Swiss eligibility requirements. The board instructs that the notarial deed be filed with the Cantonal Commercial Register without delay, that the blocked capital be released only after registration, and that this resolution be executed and minuted by all directors in compliance with Swiss law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office preliminary check via Zefix online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name availability search on the central Zefix database and in the cantonal business-name index. Draft the articles of association (Statuten) reflecting ISIC 3091 micro-mobility manufacturing, registered office, capital structure, board composition, and purpose clauses in accordance with OR Arts. 626 and 627.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is unavailable or infringing, submit an immediate name variation request and amend the draft articles prior to notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital deposit and blocked account verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank or postal financial services provider in the Canton of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the name of the future company, deposit at least CHF 50,000 paid-up capital, and obtain a formal bank confirmation confirming the funds are available and blocked for the incorporation. The confirmation must reference the company name and the founders.
required_dossiers: Founder identification and beneficial ownership declarations
AML/CFT forms from the financial intermediary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further KYC documentation, provide certified passport copies and an organizational chart of beneficial owners; re-submit within one business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal notary public (e.g., Notariat Zug or equivalent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the final articles, bank capital confirmation, and shareholder resolutions to the notary. The notary verifies legal capacity, reads the deed, obtains signatures from all incorporators, and issues the authentic notarial deed of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Authentic articles signed by all founders
Certified identity documents of all incorporators and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies incomplete foreign documentation, obtain a sworn translation or apostille within five business days or proceed with notarial verification alternatives.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons / Cantonal Commercial Register Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial deed, director declarations of office acceptance, and completeness of capital confirmation with the Commercial Register via the official cantonal submission procedure or eGR electronic filing portal. Pay the registration fee and request release of the blocked capital upon issuance of the registration certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a query or supplementation order, provide an explanatory board resolution and any missing exhibit within five business days; the registration deadline is automatically extended pending cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Gazette publication and federal compliance notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC/SHAB) and Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, the Commercial Register office arranges publication in the SOGC. Apply separately for the enterprise identification number (UID), register for VAT if taxable turnover exceeds the statutory threshold, and notify the cantonal equalization fund for old-age and survivors' insurance (AHV) if the company will employ staff.
required_dossiers: AHV and accident insurance registration forms where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the UID or VAT registration is delayed, use the provisional VAT number on invoices and correct retrospectively once the final UID is assigned.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Trade Inspectorate (Kantonales Gewerbeinspektorat) and municipal building authority (Bauamt); Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/FOEN) for federal environmental coordination.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Cantonal Betriebsbewilligung (operating permit) for manufacturing and storage premises; municipal building operating permit (Nutzungsbewilligung).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/FOEN) and Cantonal Office for the Environment of the Canton of Zug
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C – preliminary registration; a full EIA report is not mandatory for e-bike assembly unless paint-coating or metal-treatment installations exceed the VOC and wastewater thresholds of Annex 1 to the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV/OPIE).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge to municipal sewers must comply with the Waters Protection Ordinance (GSchV), generally pH 6.5–9.5 and COD limits fixed by the local wastewater utility. Coating-line exhaust must comply with the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV) total volatile organic compound limit of 100 mg/m3. Hazardous waste and lithium-ion battery handling must meet ORRChem and recovery regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate in accordance with VKF/SVTI standards (Brandschutznachweis); structural building approval and use permit from the municipal building inspectorate; workplace health and safety clearance under SECO and SUVA, including electrical installation safety inspection for battery charging and storage areas.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni), Schwanengasse 3, CH-3003 Bern; official portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch; electronic VAT service channel: SukV / VTA-Electronic via estv.admin.ch.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Procedure for a foreign-owned Swiss Aktiengesellschaft (AG) to obtain statutory tax identifiers: (1) Notarize the incorporation before a Swiss public notary; minimum share capital of CHF 100,000 must be fully subscribed with at least CHF 50,000 paid in; statutory organs (board of directors and auditor) must be identified. (2) Submit the registration application to the Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt); upon entry, the Swiss Federal Statistical Office automatically issues the Swiss UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) in the format CHE-XXX.XXX.XXX; the UID is the master tax and business identifier used for all federal, cantonal, and statistical purposes. (3) Apply for VAT registration with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration under Art. 67 of the Swiss VAT Act using the FTA registration form and the SukV electronic channel; the FTA assigns the VAT 'UID-Referenz' (MWST-Nummer), specifies the filing cycle (10.9 quarterly or annual), and issues instructions for electronic VAT return filing. (4) Register as an employer with the cantonal compensation office (AHV-Ausgleichskasse) to obtain the social security employer number. (5) The cantonal tax administration of the registered office automatically opens the cantonal and federal corporate tax account upon Commercial Register notification and dispatches the annual corporate tax return packages; no separate TIN application is required because the UID is the unique identifier. (6) A foreign-controlled AG with no effective domestic management is required to appoint a Swiss tax representative for VAT purposes; foreign shareholders and directors are permitted without domestic residency restrictions. The complete registration sequence typically takes 2 to 4 weeks after notarization.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law provides no US-style check-the-box election and no pass-through classification for an Aktiengesellschaft; the AG is a separate corporate person taxable at the entity level on worldwide net income at federal, cantonal, and communal levels. Available statutory elections and hybrid-mismatch tools: (a) VAT group taxation election (Art. 15 VAT Act) for economically integrated Swiss enterprises; (b) option under Art. 19 VAT Act to waive the exemption on real estate rental supplies in order to recover input VAT; (c) voluntary VAT registration for enterprises below the CHF 100,000 threshold (Art. 11 para 2 VAT Act); (d) participation deduction election (Art. 70 DBG and cantonal equivalents) eliminating income tax on dividends and capital gains from qualifying shareholdings of at least 10%; (e) cantonal IP-box / patent-box regimes and the notional interest deduction (NID) where election is available; and (f) hybrid mismatch consequences transposing OECD BEPS Action 2 via general anti-abuse rules, without any elective hybrid-neutralizing mechanism. No transparent or mixed-equity status is available to a Swiss AG.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual turnover (excluding VAT) of taxable supplies and services rendered by the enterprise within Swiss customs territory, plus foreign digital/telecommunications services supplied by foreign enterprises to Swiss recipients (Art. 10 para 1 and Art. 11 of the Swiss Value Added Tax Act, SR 641.20).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland has no real-time fiscal clearance model, no national digital stamping, and no invoice pre-approval API. The mandate is the issuance of invoices under Art. 26 of the Swiss VAT Act: every invoice must contain all mandatory particulars (full suppliers and buyer identity, supplier VAT/UID number, date, description of goods, quantity, tariff, consideration, VAT rate, and VAT amount) and must be issued no later than 3 months after the taxable supply. E-invoices are legally equivalent to paper; the dominant machine-readable standards are SIX eBill (pain.001/pain.002, CI-Plus) and ZUGFeRD/Factur-X. For invoices with a payment slip or payment reference, the Swiss QR-bill (QR-Rechnung) is mandatory. Federal public procurement suppliers must transmit structured electronic invoices under the OeRE Ordinance. All invoices, customs declarations, vouchers, and accounting records must be archived for 10 years under Art. 70 VAT Act; VAT returns must be filed through the FTA's electronic SukV/VTA-Electronic channel.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The zero rate applies under Art. 23 para 1 of the Swiss VAT Act to goods, including electric cargo bikes and spare parts of ISIC 3091 / HS 8711.60 and 8714.10, when the goods are physically exported from Swiss customs territory by the supplier, by the foreign customer, or by a third party on the customer's instructions, and the export is declared to Swiss customs and proven by the customs declaration certificate (Ausfuhrschein / export proof). The zero rate also covers services strictly ancillary to exported goods, such as freight, logistics, pre-export inspection, and warranty repairs on goods intended for export. Services supplied to recipients with a place of residence, establishment, or habitual residence abroad are outside the Swiss VAT scope or zero-rated under the place-of-supply rules (Art. 8/9) and Art. 23 paras 2 and 3 VAT Act. To claim recovery of input VAT embedded in the manufacturing chain, the AG must possess the export documentation package and demonstrate that the goods have not been diverted into the Swiss domestic market; the FTA accepts the zero rate only where export turnover is declared in the periodic VAT return and the transaction value is consistent with the commercial invoice.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Ausfuhrschein (official Swiss customs export certificate evidencing the zero-rated export)
Commercial Invoice with HS classification (HS 8711.60 / 8714.10) and reference to ISIC 3091 electric cargo bike manufacturing
Sales contract / purchase order naming the foreign buyer and the applicable Incoterms delivery clause
Transport document (CMR consignment note, air waybill, or carrier's certificate) demonstrating physical dispatch out of Swiss customs territory
Certificate of Origin (EUR.1/ATR or non-preferential certificate) when required by the destination country
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) may audit export zero-rating claims for up to 10 years and typically cross-checks customs extraction data, transport records, inventory movement, and the banking trail of the export proceeds. If the export proof is missing, the goods are diverted into the Swiss domestic market, or the transaction is recharacterized through an undisclosed commissionnaire or back-to-back letter-of-comfort arrangement, the FTA assesses VAT at the standard 8.1% rate on the full consideration with statutory default interest (5% per annum), denial or clawback of input VAT deductions, and retrospective reassessment of prior tax periods. Administrative fines under Art. 55/56 of the VAT Act reach up to four times the tax evaded for intentional evasion and up to one time for gross negligence; criminal prosecution under Art. 59 VAT Act may result in fines or imprisonment for responsible officers. Abusive round-tripping or fabricated export documentation also triggers the publication of judgments and the activation of international administrative-assistance and customs cooperation mechanisms. The 180-day FX repatriation benchmark represents the Swiss tax administration's arm's-length settlement norm for OEM and intercompany trade accounts; Switzerland maintains full free convertibility of the Swiss franc without an express statutory repatriation deadline.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB; German: Schweizerische Nationalbank; French: Banque nationale suisse), the central bank with exclusive CHF note-issuance and monetary policy authority. Banking supervision and enforcement are delegated to the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) under the Swiss Banking Act of 1934 and the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA), including delegated ordinances (AMLO-FINMA) on client due diligence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland is in IMF Article VIII status. The CHF is fully convertible for both current account and capital account transactions, with no quantitative ceilings, no prior SNB licensing, no minimum holding periods, and no balance-of-payments registration. Profit remittances from CH_AG to foreign shareholders are unrestricted under exchange-control law; the only material friction is the 35% Swiss anticipatory (withholding) tax on dividends and assimilated distributions, which is subject to treaty reduction or elimination under double taxation agreements and to group-autonomous relief under the revised Swiss withholding tax rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Swiss law imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender obligation for export proceeds derived from electric cargo e-bike sales. Export receipts may be retained indefinitely in CHF or foreign currency (EUR, USD, CNH) at Swiss or foreign banks; banks classify such flows for SNB statistical purposes and AML monitoring only.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CHF, EUR, USD) + Capital Escrow Account (Einzahlungskonto) + Commercial LC Facility
Operational Account + SWIFT Corporate Access + Trade Finance Line
Operational Account through Local Raiffeisen Zug
Operational Account + Wealth and Investment Backing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium, and strictly as a supplementary rail only. Foreign digital EMIs (Wise, Revolut Business, Payoneer) do not hold a FINMA banking licence and cannot act as a primary treasury counterparty for a Swiss-resident AG; their in-country operation relies on Swiss partner banks or agency segregation, creating credit and continuity risk. Legally permissible uses include small-value payouts, marketplace collections, and currency conversion convenience. Not permissible for CH_AG: holding statutory share capital for notarial confirmation, issuing UCP 600 documentary credits, providing SNB sight-deposit access, or acting as custodian for any regulated assets. A Swiss-licensed bank or a FINMA-licensed payment institution would be the minimum regulatory wrapper for treasury-as-a-service ambitions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Ukrainian law does not impose a categorical physical onboarding requirement: under FINMA Circular 2016/07 and AMLO-FINMA, remote video identification is permissible for standard-risk legal entities. However, Tier-1 Swiss banks generally condition the opening of an operational account with trade finance limits on at least one in-person interview of a signatory director and the ultimate beneficial owner at the bank's head office or branch (Zürich, Zug, or Geneva), particularly where shareholders are non-resident. Remote opening, where accepted, must use an FINMA-recognised electronic identification procedure and the bank must preserve the video record for a statutory period of ten years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owner whose tax residence is in a jurisdiction that lacks AEOI/CRS exchange or is on FATF increased-monitoring lists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified ownership-chain organigramme, notarised passport copies of each UBO, official tax-residence certificate issued by the foreign state, CRS/FATCA self-certification, a five-year bank reference from the existing relationship institution, and a sworn declaration of the legal provenance of the CHF 100,000 minimum founding capital and any paid-in surplus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-flow red flags from repetitive imports via Hong Kong/PRC agent companies for lithium-ion battery cells and electronic drive components, including invoice splitting below documentary thresholds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed purchase orders and supply agreements with final manufacturers rather than shell conduits, independent inspection certificates (SGS/TÜV/Intertek), clear Incoterms declarations, detailed HS 2022 classification sheets (electric cargo bicycles under HS 8711.60; battery packs under HS 8507.60), full customs declarations and carriage contracts, and an end-user/OEM statement confirming that goods are final-assembly urban cargo e-bikes for lawful distribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacious board control through nominee directors, minority-indirect shareholding, or escrow/founder arrangements obscuring the ultimate controller.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised shareholders' register extract, complete board minutes approving the treasury mandate, written ultimate-controller declarations under Swiss AMLA from each director, no-nominee representations, and a duplicate-signature account mandate signed at the bank's premises.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All equity injections from the foreign shareholder must be executed by SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer, with field 70 (Remittance Information) plainly reading 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION / KAPITALERHOEHUNG CH_AG' and referencing the commercial register UID (CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx). No SNB exchange-control approval or special FX form is required; the receiving Swiss bank will apply internal purpose-code classification for SNB statistical reporting and may request the notarised capital-increase resolution plus the notary's bank confirmation of the paid-up amount. For an existing company, the bank verifies the post-increase capital against the commercial register extract and confirms availability of the funds before issue of the treasury acknowledgement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for open-account settlements, advance payments, and supplier disbursements in EUR via the Swiss SEPA reachability (SIC/TARGET2 corridor) and in USD via Fedwire/CHIPS through the Swiss bank's New York correspondent; (2) Commercial documentary credits issued under UCP 600 via SWIFT MT700, with MT707 amendments and MT798 messages for LC discounting, providing secured payment against bills of lading and packing lists from the e-bike supply chain; (3) domestic CHF cash management on SIC (SIX Interbank Clearing RTGS) with 24/7 SIC-Inst for time-critical intra-Swiss payments; (4) a committed usance LC line (30-120 days) structured as trade finance to optimise liquidity. Every disbursement requires dual authorization under the Swiss signature mandate, executed via SWIFTNet corporate access or hardened e-banking tokens, and monthly reconciliation against the ERP ledger.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (USD/CHF, EUR/CHF, GBP/CHF) up to 24-month tenors documented under the Swiss Bankers Association (SBA) Master Agreement for OTC Financial Transactions, exempt from mandatory central clearing for SME-sized tickets.
FX swaps (spot vs. forward) for short-term liquidity roll-over between CHF and the EUR/USD operating currencies without balance-sheet overhang.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCS) for longer-dated project or acquisition financing, hedged with Swiss-licensed banks under ISDA or SBA documentation.
Vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars/tunnels for contingent hedging of large USD-denominated battery pack and electronics procurements.

Offshore Renminbi (CNH) deliverable forwards executed through authorised CNH market-making desks (UBS AG, HSBC Switzerland) for China/Taiwan trade payments; CHF-specific non-deliverable forwards are unnecessary and non-customary given the freely deliverable CHF market.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) approval of annual financial statements and formal minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No regulatory filing; minutes retained on-site in the corporate minute book and presented to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of fiscal year-end (Art. 699 Swiss Code of Obligations); calendar-year AG must convene by 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Board directors may incur personal liability; resolutions may be contested; continued failure to convene the AGM can trigger court-ordered corrective measures or administrative strike-off after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, notes) prepared and attached to the corporate tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Authority (federal and cantonal direct tax assessment); copy made available to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be prepared within six months after balance-sheet date; tax return generally due by 31 March following the calendar year, with canton-specific extension rules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 3–5% p.a., fines up to CHF 10,000 for late non-refund/declaration, and official estimated assessment if no return is filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss VAT annual or quarterly return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of each VAT reporting period; annual or quarterly cycle as assigned by ESTV based on turnover.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delinquency interest, administrative penalty up to CHF 10,000, compulsory assessment, and enforcement proceedings for persistent non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Auditor's report (ordinary or limited statutory audit) when the audit is not validly waived
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders at AGM; audit report is not filed with the Commercial Register unless law or special regulation so requires
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed before the AGM, ordinarily within six months of fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Board duty breach; shareholders may demand a special audit; criminal liability attaches for false certification; failure to present the report voids AGM approval in certain cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Register of Shareholders and Beneficial Owners (bearer shares) maintenance with annual verification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No regulator; register kept at the registered office and produced on request to shareholders or judicial/administrative authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuously updated upon each share transfer; verified before the AGM and annually confirmed for bearer-share beneficial owners.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines under Art. 292 Swiss Penal Code for refusing to produce the register; unrecorded beneficial owners may lose dividend and voting rights; commercial register may issue compliance orders.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A full ordinary audit is required if two of three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive years: balance-sheet total CHF 20 million; turnover CHF 40 million; average employment of 250 full-time equivalents. Below these thresholds, a limited statutory review is required unless validly waived by unanimous shareholder consent (opt-out allowed only when annual average employment ≤ 10 FTE).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957–963b) as the statutory accounting basis; Swiss GAAP FER for appropriate presentation; IFRS is permitted for listed or consolidated financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For AGs with bearer shares, beneficial owners must file a written declaration with the company; the company records and updates the UBO register on every transfer and annually reconciles it before the AGM. For registered-share AGs no annual UBO filing to an authority is required, but the board must ensure the shareholder register is current and accurate as of each general meeting.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (Board and Shareholders' Meeting Minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 – 4,500 typical annual registered-office / fiduciary-agent fee in Swiss cantons
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – 9,000 for a limited statutory review; USD 15,000 – 40,000 for a full ordinary audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal rate 8.5% of profit after tax, equivalent to 7.83% of pre-tax profit (Art. 68 DBG). With Zug cantonal and communal profit tax added, the aggregate effective rate for an ordinary manufacturing Aktiengesellschaft in the Canton of Zug is approximately 11.9%–14.6% depending on municipality and financing structure; this is below the Swiss national average of roughly 15%–17%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: STAF (Swiss Federal Act on Tax Reform and AHV Financing) 2019 measures apply: (i) Patent Box – up to 90% exemption of qualifying IP income in Zug, requiring a nexus fraction built on local R&D activities; (ii) R&D super-deduction – 150% additional deduction for R&D personnel and qualifying research costs in Zug; (iii) Notional Interest Deduction (NID) for excess equity capital, available in Zug; (iv) Participation Exemption – 95% of qualifying dividend income and capital gains from participations of ≥10% or with a market value ≥CHF 1 million are tax-exempt at federal level with full exemption at Zug cantonal level; (v) no general time-limited tax holidays for manufacturing AGs, but an orderly equity and IP holding structure lowers the effective rate toward the single-digit corridor.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Canton of Zug 'Steuererklärung für juristische Personen' (corporate tax return form) combined with the federal section 'Direkte Bundessteuer' (Kopfblatt Formular 1/1C). E-filing is available through the Canton of Zug Tax Administration e-Portal and the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) eTax system; paper filing remains accepted for the Zug corporate tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after the close of the business year (Art. 125 para. 1 DBG). For a 31 December balance-sheet date, the return and annexes must be delivered to the Zug tax authority by 30 June of the following year; extensions are granted on written application until 30 September or later. If the return is not filed within the statutory period after a reminder, the authority may estimate the taxable base at its discretion (Art. 130 para. 2 DBG) and impose a late-filing fine.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from sales of goods, works and services, net of returns and price reductions, plus inventory changes for the manufacturing operation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare worldwide turnover at arm's length value; intercompany sales to the foreign parent group must be supported by the Local File. No consolidation is allowed – only the Swiss AG's standalone legal entity result is reported.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold and material procurement, including battery and drivetrain components for the electric cargo e-bikes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party purchase prices from foreign component suppliers must satisfy the arm's length principle; add-back is required for inflated import prices that constitute a hidden profit distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Salaries, social security contributions (AHV/IV/EO/ALV/BVG), and other personnel costs of the Swiss workforce.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Remuneration of a non-resident executive director must correspond to a comparable market salary; excessive payment to a foreign shareholder would be recharacterised as a non-deductible deemed dividend.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation of tangible fixed assets recognised in the statutory books under the binding ESTV depreciation tables (machinery, rolling equipment, tooling, IT assets).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only economically justified, commercially booked depreciation is deductible; the tax authority may adjust depreciation rates based on the useful economic life of the e-bike production equipment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses: federal/cantonal income tax, capital tax, fines, political contributions, client entertainment in excess of statutory limits, and hidden profit distributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 35% Swiss anticipatory tax is a shareholder-level tax and is not deductible by the AG; transfer pricing adjustments and deemed distributions must be consistently added back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net profit according to Swiss accounting law (OR Art. 958e) before loss offset, after all statutory add-backs and exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the starting point of the tax computation; non-resident shareholders should verify that the audited financial statements contain no unreported related-party transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of proven tax loss carry-forwards of the preceding 7 assessment periods (Art. 211 DBG).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses from foreign permanent establishments and losses of foreign group companies are not eligible; a clear loss register in CHF must be attached to the tax return file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net income for the direkt Bundessteuer after loss offset, before the participation deduction and patent box relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The cantonal/communal taxable income is calculated on the same base but multiplied by the Zug tax factors; non-resident shareholders should confirm the equality of the federal and Cantonal computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption deduction for qualifying dividends and capital gains from participations held at ≥10% or with a value of at least CHF 1 million (Art. 69 DBG).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Keep proof of the participation percentage and acquisition cost; the 5% deemed non-deductible expense ratio (2% effective after the STAF amendment) automatically applies to the gross exempt income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Patent box relief for net qualifying income from patents and analogous rights, calculated using the R&D nexus ratio recognised by the Canton of Zug.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Requires a prior ruling with the Zug tax authority and evidence that the qualifying R&D activities are performed by Swiss employees; license-in intangible rights from the foreign parent are generally not eligible for the box.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing: (i) default assessment by the tax office under discretionary estimation (Art. 130 DBG); (ii) procedural fine of up to CHF 10,000 (Art. 174 DBG) for violation of filing duties; (iii) late-payment default interest on the outstanding tax (approx. 3%–4.5% p.a.); (iv) intentional false statements trigger criminal tax evasion proceedings under Art. 175 DBG with fines of 1–3 times the evaded tax, and, in aggravated document-based fraud cases, imprisonment of up to 2 years (Art. 186 DBG) or up to 5 years for VAT fraud. Travel bans and asset seizure may be attached in criminal proceedings.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% anticipatory tax (Verrechnungssteuer) levied on distributions of the Swiss AG to all shareholders, resident and non-resident alike (Art. 13 VStG). The AG is obliged to withhold and remit the tax before the dividend is paid; payment without withholding shifts the tax liability to the company and its board.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must file a refund claim with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) in Berne, generally using Form 82/85, within 3 years after the end of the calendar year in which the dividend became due. The application must attach (i) the Tax Residence Certificate (Ansässigkeitsbescheinigung) issued by the foreign tax authority of the shareholder, (ii) the dividend voucher or bank confirmation evidencing the distribution and the 35% tax withheld, (iii) proof of the shareholding percentage and holding period, and (iv) a beneficial-ownership statement. Under the Germany–Switzerland DTA (1971 as amended by the 2010 Protocol) a German corporate parent holding at least 10% of the capital unconditionally during an uninterrupted period of 12 months obtains a 0% Swiss dividend WHT (full refund of the 35%); portfolio dividends of below 10% remain limited to 15%. For other DTA partners the rate is commonly 5% (direct investment) or 15% (portfolio), and zero under several post-2010 treaties. Banks may apply the ESTV notification procedure (Meldeverfahren) for listed Swiss securities; for an unlisted manufacturing AG, the refund procedure is the sole standard route. The documentation package should include a Limitation-on-Benefits / principal purpose test analysis where the treaty so requires.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Swiss source taxation: ordinary intercompany and bank interest, trade interest and royalties are generally outside the scope of the 35% anticipatory tax and may be paid gross, provided the debt is not structured as a taxable Swiss debenture (obligation) and the royalty relates to industrial or commercial IP without Swiss real estate nexus. Interest on Swiss-issued bond-like instruments triggers the 35% tax. Treaty protection (Germany–Switzerland DTA as amended): royalties are taxable only in the state of residence of the beneficial owner (0% source tax); interest likewise attracts 0% source tax if paid to a beneficial owner resident in the other state at arm's length, with a back-to-back anti-abuse recharacterisation under the 2010 Protocol. The refund of any excess tax withheld is applied for through the same ESTV refund mechanism as dividends.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Switzerland has no separate TP documentation statute, but the ESTV's Kreisschreiben Nr. 13 (12 June 2020) obliges taxpayers to apply the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines and to prepare contemporaneous documentation. The ESTV expects a Local File where annual related-party transactions exceed approximately CHF 5 million (goods and services) or CHF 1 million (financing transactions); a Master File is expected for significant intra-group flows, and a Country-by-Country Report is mandatory for multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue of CHF 900 million or more. The Zug-based e-bike manufacturer with cross-border component purchases and IP licences should prepare and file the transfer pricing documentation with the annual tax return once the thresholds are met, and earlier if any related-party transaction is material, to pre-empt recharacterisation of income.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No standalone Swiss ESR code exists, but economic substance is legally decisive in four fields. (i) Seat and management: under Art. 56 ZGB and Art. 643 OR, the AG must maintain a real registered office in Switzerland and its effective management (board meetings, strategic decisions) must occur in Switzerland; absence of these facts shifts the residence of the company and the taxing right abroad. (ii) Eligibility for tax incentives: the patent box, R&D super-deduction and NID require the taxpayer itself to perform the qualifying R&D or to finance the qualifying assets with substance performing a business purpose. (iii) Treaty entitlement: letterbox companies are denied the DTA benefits under the MLI principal purpose test and the specific anti-abuse clauses of the Swiss DTA network. (iv) Capital tax: the Zug capital tax assessments will verify that equity is genuinely employed in operating assets and not merely held to claim the NID. For a manufacturing AG with physical plant, production employees and board meetings in Zug, substance is established per se; using a nominee board, an empty registered address, or an artificial cash box would fail these tests and trigger reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Tax Fraud (Steuerhinterziehung / Steuerbetrug)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing materially false Swiss income and capital tax returns: under-declaring sales of electric cargo e-bikes, fabricating costs of imported components, omitting related-party income, or destroying accounting records to reduce the taxable base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines of 1–3 times the amount of the evaded federal tax (Art. 175 DBG); additional cantonal fines in Zug; default interest on the full underpaid amount; where false or forged documents are used to deceive the tax authority, criminal tax fraud under Art. 186 DBG carries imprisonment of up to 2 years, while VAT fraud under Art. 105 MWSTG carries imprisonment of up to 5 years. The entire reassessment may cover the full 10-year limitation period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members, the CEO and the responsible CFO face personal criminal liability; the corporate veil is pierced for deliberate evasion. Sanctions include personal fines, disgorgement of unlawful profits, asset seizures, travel bans, and imprisonment. In addition, the executives are jointly liable for the unpaid withholding tax and for the company's tax debt attributable to their breach of fiduciary duties (OR Art. 754).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abusive Letterbox Substance Deficiency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Swiss AG as a pure domiciliary vehicle with a registered office but no premises, staff, accounting substance or actual board activity, while claiming treaty benefits, the participation exemption, the patent box or the Zug NID, or while channelling profits through Switzerland without operational purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief: the 0% or 5% dividend/interest/royalty treaty rate is revoked and the full 35% anticipatory tax becomes finally exigible; the participation exemption is refused; cantonal and federal reassessment for up to 10 years; additional fines for negligent or intentional tax evasion of up to 3 times the additional tax; the commercial register may also initiate compulsory dissolution of the abusively structured entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The signatories of the tax return are personally liable for the non-withheld 35% anticipatory tax under Art. 12 VStG. Directors who certify false substance or sign abusive rulings are exposed to criminal liability for false certification under Art. 251 StGB (imprisonment up to 3 years) and to civil restitution actions of the tax authority. Travel bans and freezing orders apply in pending investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Hidden Profit Distribution and Non-Arm's Length Related-Party Flows (Verdeckte Gewinnausschüttung)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying inflated licence, management, purchasing or financing fees to the foreign parent, granting interest-free shareholder loans, or pricing e-bike component sales below the arm's length band, thereby draining Swiss profit without a formal dividend resolution and without withholding the 35% anticipatory tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The excess amount is recharacterised as a deemed dividend: (i) the Swiss AG loses the deduction, (ii) the 35% anticipatory tax becomes payable on the deemed distribution, and (iii) interest and evasion penalties of 1–3 times the evaded tax under Art. 13 VStG apply. Transfer pricing corrections are simultaneously imposed at federal and Zug cantonal level, including capital tax recalculations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The board members are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid 35% withholding tax (Art. 12 VStG). Deliberate structuring of such payments constitutes disloyalty and criminal mismanagement under Art. 158 StGB, punishable by imprisonment of up to 3 years; the shareholders are subject to civil restitution of the distributed amounts, and the executives to professional bans and asset seizure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Unlicensed Payment or Crypto-Facilitation Activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting customer or business partner payments in cryptocurrency or acting as a payment intermediary or crypto broker without registration with a Swiss self-regulatory organisation (SRO) and without FINMA licensing under the AMLA or FinIA; alternatively processing wire transfers to shell beneficiaries or sanctioned jurisdictions while bypassing the bank's KYC/AML controls. The standard Swift LC / TT Wire payment structure of the e-bike manufacturer is low-risk, but any unauthorised crypto acceptance in the Zug ecosystem triggers this compliance exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of the AMLA constitutes a criminal offence: fines of up to CHF 500,000 for negligence and up to CHF 1,000,000 plus imprisonment of up to 3 years for intentional breach (Art. 39–40 AMLA). FINMA may revoke the registration, order cessation of business, appoint an investigating agent, and in DNAB proceedings require the disgorgement of profits. The entity may be struck from the commercial register if it operates without the required licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the compliance officer are personally subject to criminal prosecution under the AMLA and StGB Art. 165; FINMA bans the individuals from exercising management activities in the financial sector, imposes personal disgorgement, and may refer the matter to the criminal authorities with the consequence of travel bans, asset blocking and imprisonment up to 3 years. Directors who knowingly allow unlicensed crypto acceptance are additionally liable for all resulting damages under company law (OR Art. 754).
